# 01 An arrow token decomposes into a line, two ends, and a length

## Outcome

`---`, `-.->`, `-.-`, `==>`, `===`, `--o`, `--x`, `<-->` and the long forms all parse, lay out and
draw as what they are: a line style, an end on each side, and a distance.

## Why this ticket exists

Seven of the corpus's nine edge rows, and the mechanism the other two hang off. `GraphEdge` is
`{ id, from, to, style }` today — every one of these forms is one contract change away.

**Decompose, do not enumerate.** `A <-.-> B` is not a fourteenth arrow name; it is a dotted line
with an arrow on each end. This repo has made that call twice already — `SequenceArrow
{ line, head }` and `ClassRelationship`'s `fromEnd`/`toEnd`, where the class renderer already draws
five endpoint shapes on either end of a line and mints a marker per shape. **Read
`renderClassDiagramToSVG`'s `END_MARKER_NAME` before you design anything**; a third vocabulary for
the same idea would be the drift three boards have now been spent removing.

A long arrow is the one form that is not about drawing. `A ----> B` puts its target further down
the rank order in Mermaid, so it reaches dagre as `minlen`. Drawing all lengths alike would be a
silent mis-render by the corpus's own definition; refusing long arrows would breach the absolute
condition. The spec's decision 2 explains why honoring it is the only option left.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `contracts.ts` gains `EdgeLine` and `EdgeEnd`; `GraphEdge` gains `line`, `fromEnd`, `toEnd`
      and a length. **Required, not optional** — `A --> B` is `solid` / `none` / `arrow` / 1, so a
      plain arrow is one state rather than two, matching `style` and `shape`.
- [x] Every token in the corpus's seven rows parses to the right decomposition. **Measure which end
      each token marks with the probe** rather than recalling it — `--o` and `--x` in particular.
- [x] `A ----> B` reaches dagre as a longer `minlen`, and the drawn diagram differs from
      `A --> B`'s. Assert it at the **layout** seam against node coordinates, not only that it
      rendered — the claim is about rank position.
- [x] Each end draws its own marker, on the correct side. `<-->` needs `marker-start` as well as
      `marker-end`; the class renderer does exactly this and is the template.
- [x] **The marker matrix is keyed by (shape, colour) and minted only for pairs a diagram
      actually draws.** Board 3 mints per colour so a styled edge's whole arrow takes it; ends now
      have shapes too. A document with one colour and one head shape must still emit one marker —
      assert that, because an unbounded matrix is the obvious wrong turn.
- [x] A dotted and a thick line are visibly different from a solid one and from each other. Decide
      how (`stroke-dasharray`, `stroke-width`, a class) and say why; whatever you choose must not
      collide with an author's `linkStyle 0 stroke-width:…`, which already lands on the same
      element. State what happens when it does.
- [x] Every styled and animated edge still works: `linkStyle` still lands, `timeline:` still moves
      the edge, and the marker still takes the author's colour.
- [x] Seven corpus rows move to `supported`, each asserting the drawn line and ends. Expect
      `REJECTED` 22 → **15**; the number is an expectation, not a quota. `SILENTLY_WRONG` stays at
      **3** and its rows are not this board's.

## Status

Done (2026-09-08), commit dc2baee. 7 slices (5 red-green, 2 proven by mutation).
784 core tests / 29 board, tsc clean both, both build.
Ratchets: rejected 22 → **15**, silently-wrong untouched at **3**. Corpus 55 / 15 / 3.

Everything measured against mermaid 11.17.2 including its `destructEdgeType` source. Two rows added
(`-.-`, `===`) that no probe had recorded — an instrument gap, so they do not lower the number.

**The line style is a class, not inline**, because inline would have beaten `highlight X outline`
too and silently stopped thickening a thick edge — on an element that is a timeline target.

## Test seam

`parseFlowchart` through the source string; `layoutGraph` for `minlen`; `render()` for the drawn
line and markers; the corpus.
